slides.say: The operation diamond is defined for every even integer x that's zero or more. Diamond of x is two when x is zero, and nine minus diamond of x minus two when x is two or more. Diamond of six is equal to what?
A circular rule, the operation appears inside its own definition. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, going down and back up, and then with the pattern.
[short pause] Diamond of six is nine minus diamond of four. We don't know that yet, so keep going. Diamond of four is nine minus diamond of two.
Diamond of two is nine minus diamond of zero. And diamond of zero is given, two. Now only numbers are left.
Climb back up. Nine minus two is seven, so diamond of two is seven. Nine minus seven is two. And nine minus two is seven. Diamond of six is seven. Choice number four is our answer.
at: Choice number four is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way. What's different? We look for the pattern instead of climbing every step. Two, seven, two, seven. Zero, four and eight give two, and two and six give seven. So six gives seven, choice number four, and even diamond of a hundred would be instant. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
